conventions.affine: 4x4 row-major [row][col]; maps voxel (i,j,k,1) -> world RAS mm (ARCHITECTURE.md §3)
conventions.meshElementNumbers: 1-based Gmsh element numbers (§6.2); tris are the first block
conventions.meshFormats: §6.2's VTK legacy / VTK XML / OFF / MEDIT fixtures; `gmsh` = the Gmsh 4.14 Python API (legacy .vtk, .off, .mesh only), `meshio` = meshio (all nine)
conventions.spotValues: raw = on-disk sample; physical = raw*sclSlope+sclInter (never folded, §6.1)
conventions.voxelOrder: i fastest, then j, then k, then volume index

description: Ground truth for the committed synthetic fixtures in testdata/. Every number here was produced by an INDEPENDENT reader — nibabel for NIfTI/GIfTI/FreeSurfer (MGH/MGZ included), SimpleITK for NRRD/MetaImage (loaded in LPS, stored here as RAS), simnibs.mesh_io.read_msh for Gmsh v2.2, the Gmsh 4.14 Python API for Gmsh v4.1, for STL/PLY/OBJ and for legacy VTK/OFF/MEDIT, meshio for VTK legacy+XML/OFF/MEDIT — never by the writer in scripts/gen-fixtures.py. Regenerate with `python3 scripts/gen-fixtures.py`.

lattice_binary.vtk.readerNote: Gmsh 4.14 cannot load a BINARY legacy .vtk (not even one it wrote itself), so meshio is the only independent reader here; lattice_ascii.vtk is the same lattice and carries the Gmsh record.

patch.vtp.readerNote: meshio refused the file (meshio has no .vtp reader); patch_polydata.vtk holds the same 16 vertices and 9 quads and Gmsh reads that one — its record is copied here as expectedFromEquivalentLegacy.

patch_polydata.vtk.readerNote: meshio refused the file (meshio's legacy reader supports UNSTRUCTURED_GRID only, not POLYDATA); the Gmsh record is the ground truth.

patch_quad.off.readerNote: meshio refused the file (meshio's OFF reader reads triangular faces only); the Gmsh record is the ground truth.

notGenerated.instead: crates/tvx-geom/tests/fixtures.rs::big_node_count_mesh() builds one in memory at test time (a k x k x 1 grid of shared-vertex tets), and the real-data test uses m2m_ernie/ernie_seeg.msh (2,301,899 nodes, 22 bits) per AGENTS.md.
notGenerated.what: a mesh with >= 2**21 nodes for §11's face-key-width test
notGenerated.why: 2,097,152 nodes is ~25 MB of coordinates and ~100 MB of tets; there is no encoding of it that fits the 2 MB committed-fixture budget.

notGenerated.instead: the Rust test truncates vol_u8.nii's magic to `ni1\0` in memory.
notGenerated.why: §6.1 rejects it by name (Error::Unsupported("two-file NIfTI")); no valid fixture is needed to assert a rejection.

notGenerated.instead: the Rust tests rewrite an attached fixture's header in memory.
notGenerated.what: a detached-header NRRD (.nhdr) or MetaImage (.mhd), or a bzip2 NRRD
notGenerated.why: §6.1 rejects them by name; the byte-slice signature has no sibling-file access and bzip2 is not a dependency.

notGenerated.instead: the Rust test rewrites surf_ascii.surf.gii's Encoding attribute in memory.
notGenerated.why: §6.2 rejects it by name; the byte-slice signature has no sibling-file access.

patch_ascii.stl.readerNote: STL has no vertex table. Gmsh welds coincident vertices (weldedNodes); a non-welding reader produces unweldedVertices instead. Either is contract-legal for read_stl (§6.2); the triangle count and the bbox are the invariants.

patch_binary.stl.readerNote: STL has no vertex table. Gmsh welds coincident vertices (weldedNodes); a non-welding reader produces unweldedVertices instead. Either is contract-legal for read_stl (§6.2); the triangle count and the bbox are the invariants.

patch_quad_ascii.ply.readerNote: Gmsh 4.14's PLY reader truncates each quad to its first three indices, so the numbers above are Gmsh's, NOT what a correct reader must produce. The file holds the same 16 vertices and 9 quads as patch_quad.obj; use that entry (Gmsh reads OBJ n-gons correctly, element type 3) as the expectation for read_ply.

conventions.box: half-extent ceil(radiusMm / spacing) voxels PER AXIS, clipped to the volume, capped at 32 voxels on an axis (ARCHITECTURE.md §4.3)
conventions.peakCentroid: weights clip(v - (max - 0.5*(max - min)), 0); centroid in voxel indices, then through the affine
conventions.spotValues: offset is [i, j, k] within the box; i fastest, like VolumeDataset.data
conventions.values: physical = raw * sclSlope + sclInter, applied once

voxelBox.groundTruth: nibabel + numpy, reading ct_shafts.nii.gz back (the shaft geometry is authored)
